gao-gaoreports-gao-07-731g:
Government Auditing Standards, in the July 2007 revision numbered GAO-07-731G, sets the rules for audits of public funds. The book is known as the Yellow Book. It supersedes the 2003 revision. Auditors who follow it work for federal, state, and local bodies. It covers financial audits, attestation work, and performance audits. One part lays out rules for reporting on internal control.

Early chapters set ethics rules, such as integrity, objectivity, and care with public resources. They also demand independence, sound judgment, and staff skill. Later chapters give field work and reporting rules for each audit type. Appendices add extra guidance on how to apply the standards. Audit shops use the book to plan work and write reports. Its rules shape how findings on waste, fraud, and weak controls reach the public.
podcast-tuckercarlson-fxWZO0FEQ1g:
Analyst Luke Gromen joins Tucker Carlson to praise gold at a time of tech hype. Gromen notes that nations spend huge sums buying the metal. Every culture, he says, has trusted gold for six thousand years.

He argues gold works when times turn spicy and trust fails. The title asks if the CIA fears public gold ownership. It also asks if Fort Knox hides the true reserve count. Gromen lays out a case for hard money. The episode suits savers who doubt paper wealth and want an old asset explained clearly.
